messages:
ashley_r: Heads-up — nightly stress on 8xA100 (tensor+pipeline mix) shows allreduce latency slowly drifting up across long runs. Start step 1-2k p50 ~2.1ms, by step 30k p50 ~6.4ms. p99 spikes even worse.

mike_w: ugh. same job or new config? any KV-cache changes or batching tweaks?

ashley_r: same config as last stable. no KV changes, batch sizes constant. We saw a pattern where when LL128 is enabled, after some time a subset of ranks switch to proto algo for >8MB messages. suspect NCCL falling back due to connection/resource pressure.

kevin_o: did you capture NCCL logs? try set NCCL_DEBUG=INFO and NCCL_ALGO=ring,tree? also NCCL_PROTO=LL to force?

ashley_r: Attached snippet from the worker logs (redacted):

```
NCCL INFO: Using LL128
NCCL WARNING: algo switch detected on rank 3: proto selected for allreduce size=9.4MB
allreduce(A): step=12034 duration=6.12ms
allreduce(A): step=30005 duration=6.78ms
```

tara_s: perf-bot flagged a regression earlier today (5% p99 across serving jobs). linking profiler traces in case: /perf/artifacts/179802/trace-ll128-drift.pbz.

perf-bot: regression_alert: job="nightly-multi-gpu-stress" metric="allreduce_p50" delta="+210%" span="last_7_days"

mike_w: I wonder if there is microburst / NIC ring buffer exhaustion causing fallback to proto. When LL128 paths see retransmits or cq timeouts the driver might force a different protocol. Also if channels share same NIC QPs they can outlive socket limits.

kevin_o: hypothesis list: 1) progressive fragmentation of cached comms (we keep reusing communicators and NN ops grow) 2) NCCL internal heuristics detect poorer peer latency and fallback to proto 3) GPU churn (ECC/memory errors) causing rank slowdowns and unevenness triggers algo change.

ashley_r: Repro script and env we used:

```
# repro snippet
export NCCL_DEBUG=INFO
export NCCL_ALGO=DEFAULT
export NCCL_PROTO=LL128
export NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME=eth0
mpirun -np 8 --bind-to none --map-by slot ./run_infer_stress.sh --batch 2 --seq 2048
```

mike_w: can you try forcing NCCL_ALGO=ring and NCCL_PROTO=LL (not LL128) for a run and compare allreduce histogram? If the drift goes away it's likely LL128-specific path.

tara_s: I ran a short check on 4xH100 for 10k steps forcing ring+LL. initial numbers look more stable p50 ~2.3ms -> 2.5ms at 10k, no header fallback logs. Uploading diff: /perf/diffs/179802/h100-ring-ll.json

ashley_r: good. Also noticed KV-cache pressure: when prefix cache hit rate drops we see more KV fetches concurrently which slightly increase payloads (more >8MB collective messages). Could push NCCL over the threshold where proto is chosen.

kevin_o: possible mitigation ideas: - periodic communicator reinit (every N steps) to clear stale connections - cap collective message sizes via chunking at runtime (split into smaller allreduces) - tune NIC buffers / increase OS ulimit for fds - experiment with NCCL_MAX_RINGS / NCCL_MAX_SOCKETS envs

mike_w: also add an opt-in adaptive fallback policy in runtime: if we detect persistent algo-switch to proto, switch batching heuristic to smaller micro-batches for a cooling period. That reduces message size and should nudge NCCL back to LL128.

ashley_r: I'll run: 1) forced ring+LL run (48h), 2) LL128 with periodic communicator refresh every 5k steps, 3) LL128 + batch cap at 6MB. Will gather traces and perf-bot will re-evaluate.

perf-bot: scheduled: compare_runs: [1798023345/force-ring-ll, 1798023345/refresh-comms, 1798023345/ll128-batchcap] window=48h

tara_s: small ask — when you share traces, include nvtx ranges for allreduce start/stop and the NCCL log around the same step. Makes correlation much faster.

ashley_r: noted. I'll attach nvprof ranges + NCCL logs for suspected steps (12k, 30k). Also adding a perf counter capture of NIC retries.

kevin_o: if we confirm LL128 fragility under sustained KV/large-message mix, file a runtime ticket to prefer proto for >X MB when contended, and otherwise keep LL128 with aggressive health checks. Save LL128 perf for steady-state low-jitter loads.

mike_w: sounds good. Thanks for digging in — this explains a lot of the sporadic regression alerts. Ping me when first forced-run finishes and I'll help parse the traces. :thumbsup:

ashley_r: Will do.
